messages:
alex: quick one — running into 401s in our RN app after we rotate ephemeral tokens. works for first request, then subsequent calls from WKWebView fetch get 401s. anyone seen this?
maya: hosted or private? and which SDK (web vs RN native)?
alex: hosted. using our JS RN SDK inside a WebView (react-native-webview). we create ephemeral token server-side and set it in window.fetch headers. initial stream works then later fails.
tom: RN WebView + WKWebView can be weird with headers — sometimes preflight caching or injected JS stuck with old closure var. are you mutating a global token var?
alex: yes we set window._token and our fetch reads that. we also refresh via setInterval 30s before expiry and update window._token. snippet: 
```
fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + token,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-medium', input:'hi'})
});
```
samir: streaming in RN webview is fragile. RN fetch often buffers until complete and doesnt surface chunked SSE. also WKWebView can cache preflight results. try appending a cache-bust header or change header value on refresh.
donna: also check you dont have a service worker inside the webview intercepting requests and rewriting headers. that bit caught us before.
maya: for mobile we usually recommend native wrappers for streaming (Swift/Kotlin) that handle token rotation at the transport layer. if you must use WebView, ensure you re-create the webview context on token rotation or re-inject the updated auth header right before request.
alex: curious about native approach — any example for Swift/Kotlin how to swap token without dropping UX?
tom: Swift pseudocode: 
```
// set token on client
client.setAuthToken(token) // thread-safe
// when token refreshed
client.updateAuthToken(newToken)
// if stream is long-lived, close+reopen with new token
client.closeStream();
client.openStream();
```

Kotlin similar. aim to rotate before you open long streams. if token expires mid-stream, graceful reconnect is best.
maya: CORS note: browser clients need the API to allow your origin and expose Authorization header. config: 
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type
Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Link, X-Request-Id
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true (if using cookies)

infra-bot: deploy-bot: applied ingress rule to rwinf-prod to allow origin https://app.example.com at 2025-07-22T15:04Z

alex: got it. one more — streaming socket sometimes closes with 499 when token refresh happens. should client re-open automatically?
samir: yes — implement reconnect with backoff on 4xx/5xx close codes that look auth-related. treat token-refresh as expected lifecycle event and reopen. also emit metric for 401-after-refresh.
sre-jen: ^ please add alert for spike in post-refresh 401s, add a dashboard.
maya: i'll open a PR to add native token bridge + auto-reconnect to RN SDK, plus docs for WebView caveats. @tom can you review?
tom: sure — will review #3292 today.
alex: awesome, thanks folks :rocket: this helps a lot.
maya: good call — adding a short snippet to docs about streaming+rotation and preferred native path. :+1:
